title: Watchdog focusing on two London police officers after in-custody death of Amanda Bolt, 28
article: Ontario's police watchdog is probing the conduct of two London police officers in the case of a woman who died in hospital 10 days after being found unresponsive in a police cell.
Amanda Bolt, 28, was found without vital signs in a cell at police headquarters on Nov. 2.

Bolt, who had been arrested the previous day on a failure to comply charge, was administered Naloxone - a nasal spray that can reverse the symptoms of opioid drug overdoses - before she was taken to the hospital, where she died on Nov. 13.

Police notified the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) of the incident, but the watchdog initially said it was monitoring the woman's condition and hadn't invoked its mandate. The watchdog announced it had opened an investigation on Nov. 18, but it didn't say how many officers would be the subject of its probe.
The agency is investigating the conduct of two officers, neither of whom was identified, spokesperson Monica Hudon said Thursday.
Four officers have been designated witnesses, Hudon said.
Officers under investigation by the SIU aren't legally required to turn over their notes or be subjected to an interview.
Created in 1990, the SIU probes all cases of death, serious injuries and allegations of sexual assault involving police.
The SIU has opened 10 cases involving London police this year: five remain open, four were closed without any charges and one resulted in a charge of assault causing bodily harm against an officer.
Bolt, whose cause of death hasn't been made public, had battled drug addiction and had run-ins with police for years, but her family say her struggles didn't define her.
Around 75 people attended a celebration of life for Bolt last Saturday in Port Stanley.
